$comment: Free tiers change often. Limits here are conservative defaults checked on 2026-10-29; a 429 from the provider always wins over these numbers. PRs that update a limit should say where the number came from. Stealth models (beam, glyph-cluster) are ranked by a live Persian probe on 2026-10-29, not by a published benchmark.

providers.name: Kilo Gateway
providers.privacy: Free models come from many upstreams. Kilo's docs say NVIDIA's free endpoints log prompts (trial use only) and its auto-free router may use providers that log. Do not send secrets or personal data.
providers.note: Anonymous use is 200 requests an hour per IP (Kilo gateway docs, 2026-10).

providers.name: OVHcloud AI Endpoints
providers.privacy: Hosted in the EU. OVHcloud says AI Endpoints data is not used for training and is not stored; its pages do not say whether that covers anonymous calls.
providers.note: Anonymous use is 2 requests a minute per IP and per model, every chat model is free that way. A token from a paid Public Cloud project raises it to 400; set limits.rpm in your config if you have one.

providers.name: Groq
providers.privacy: Says it does not train on API inputs.

providers.name: OpenRouter
providers.privacy: Each free model is served by a different upstream with its own policy; several log prompts.
providers.note: 50 requests a day for the whole account. A one-time 10 USD top-up raises it to 1000; set limits.rpd in your config if you did that.

providers.name: Google Gemini
providers.privacy: The free tier uses your prompts to improve Google products.
providers.note: Google blocks some accounts by the country they were registered in, even behind a VPN.

providers.name: Mistral
providers.privacy: The free Experiment plan may require opting in to data use. Check the current terms.

providers.name: Cloudflare Workers AI
providers.privacy: Says it does not train on customer content.
providers.note: The free allowance is 10,000 neurons a day, which is not a request count. Expect a 429 when it runs out.
